rounds.headline: Stop writing unused DeltaNet state snapshots; replay accepted rows instead.
rounds.hypothesis: A verify step of T rows wrote T fp32 state snapshots (3.15 MB each, 48 layers = 0.6 GB at T=4, 1.2 GB at T=8) of which only the accepted row's was ever read. nsys: DeltaNet kernels are 1.38 ms of a 21.7 ms cycle at 650-680 GB/s, dominated by snapshot writes. Deferring the snapshots (save per-row k, v, gate, beta; replay accepted rows at the start of the next DeltaNet step) cuts the traffic from 1 read + T writes to 1 read + 1 write per layer. Measured: DeltaNet kernel 23.0->21.5 us at T=4 and 41.6->31.2 us at T=8, cycle 21.66->21.43 ms (profile), check PASS; the kernel is shuffle/latency bound so the gain is smaller than the traffic model.

rounds.headline: Repack 4-bit weights into tile-contiguous layout so GPU matrix-vector kernels stream memory faster
rounds.hypothesis: GEMV_LOG #10 measured -3% GEMV time in the lab (-0.21 ms T=1, -0.45 ms T=4 per step) from tile-contiguous 1 KB units, one u32 scale per (tile, group, row pair) and natural nibble order (no activation permutes); only the weight layout/addressing differs, outputs equal up to mma k order.

rounds.headline: DeltaNet verify steps store tiny rank-1 updates instead of full state snapshots, replayed lazily.
rounds.hypothesis: Verify T=4..8 DeltaNet wrote (1+T) x 3.15 MB per layer (1.14 ms at T=4, 2.0 ms at T=8 for 48 layers); the recurrence S_t = ge*S_{t-1} + d (x) k is exactly replayable, so only the deltas (~33 KB/row) need storing; measured per-layer kernel 23.7->18.7 us at T=4 and 41->28 us at T=8 (profile), plus occasional flush.
rounds.change: src/deltanet.cu: lazy kernel MODE 1/2 (per-layer 2x16-row delta buffer, pending count|base|half in ds[19], bitwise replay in smem, flush of start state only when buffer full) + materialize kernel; engine.cu/mtp_sample.h/mtp.cu/prefill.cu/prefill.py: pending bookkeeping in accept/advance kernels, materialize before snapshot and python prefill; swiftmk_deltanet_step contract unchanged.

rounds.hypothesis: k_bf16_small (in_proj_a|b, forked graph branch) used 184 registers x 128 threads = 23.5k regs per CTA, while two resident k_w4 CTAs leave only 16k registers per SM, so the fork could not co-reside with the qkv|z GEMV and serialised (~0.47 ms/cycle of nsys kernel time). Also the RMSNorm weight load is issued before the reduction (2.8 -> 2.6 us x 135 launches). # cycle2 lab notebook (focus: MTP cycle overhead, small kernels outside the verify GEMVs)

## Profile of the inherited state (try --profile, prompt code, 32 cycles, 20.541 ms/cycle wall, 3.906 tok/cycle)
GEMV k_w4 17.95 ms (275 launches), DeltaNet 1.09, k_bf16_small (in_proj_a|b) 0.473 (48 x 9.8 us), rmsnorm 0.365 (135 x 2.7 us),
attention split 0.30 + prep 0.059 + reduce 0.055, head select/rescore ~0.03, everything else < 0.02. Sum of kernels 20.3 ms vs 20.54 wall: gaps are only ~0.2 ms/cycle.

## Idea 0: programmatic dependent launch (griddepcontrol) to hide ramp/tail between kernels
Expected: 0.3-0.8 ms (prefetch of weights before the wait). Concluded: not possible. PTX `griddepcontrol` needs sm_90+, this is an sm_86 RTX 3090. Not tried.

## Idea 1: k_bf16_small (in_proj_a|b) uses 184 registers x 128 threads
Observation: the two resident k_w4 CTAs/SM (92 regs -> 96 allocated x 256 thr x 2) leave 16384 registers per SM; one k_bf16_small CTA needs 23552, so the forked
a|b branch cannot co-reside with the qkv|z GEMV and effectively serialises (9.8 us avg per call in nsys vs 6.5 us solo).
Change: `__launch_bounds__(128, 8)` -> 64 registers, 0 spills (cuobjdump). Expected: up to -0.3..0.4 ms/cycle (1.5-2%).
Measured (try --profile, code prompt, 32 cycles, ms/cycle wall): inherited 20.541 -> 20.375 (-0.8%); k_bf16_small now overlaps (14.0 us in nsys, off the critical path). Kept.

## Idea 2: rmsnorm loads the norm weight before the reduction (hide its latency), 135 launches x 2.8 us
Expected: -0.3..0.5 us per launch = -0.04..0.07 ms/cycle (0.2-0.3%). Measured: rmsnorm 2.8 -> 2.6 us avg (0.372 -> 0.354 ms/cycle, profile). Kept (small).

## Idea 3: split qkv|z GEMV, run the z projection (15.7 MB) on the side stream concurrently with the latency-bound DeltaNet kernel (DN uses ~150 GB/s of 880), gated RMSNorm tail moved into its own kernel
Expected: hide ~15 us per DeltaNet layer = up to -0.7 ms/cycle (3%).
Variant A (z GEMV = cfg 3 w4k4u3, auto grid 192): wall 20.662 ms/cycle (worse than 20.375): z GEMV 27.4 us, DN 20.3 -> 24.6 us, gnorm kernel 2.4 us.
Variant B (z GEMV cfg 3 with grid 96, so DN CTAs keep SM resources): wall 20.934 ms/cycle (worse), z 32.6 us, DN 20.7 us (unchanged), qkv GEMV -19 us.
Concluded: no useful overlap between the z GEMV and DeltaNet on this GPU/graph (section time ~ qkv + DN + z + gnorm = sum, not max). Reverted (deltanet.cu, engine.cu, gemv.cu grid override).

## Final state (this session)
Kept: k_bf16_small launch bounds (128, 8) + k_rmsnorm weight prefetch. Full try: main 175.37 tok/s (code 181.3 prose 113.1 math 180.1 long8k 141

# dnet2 lab notebook (DeltaNet kernel after the lazy rank-1 replay)

Baseline profile (nsys, 32 `code` cycles, ms/cycle): dn_kernel T=4 20.3 us x 33 calls, T=8 29.2 us x 15 calls -> DeltaNet total 1.106 ms of a 20.4 ms cycle (5.4%).

## 1. Row-per-lane-group layout + transposed warp reductions
- Expected: the old layout (lane = 4 K-elements of 4 rows, 5-level butterfly per value) needed 40 shuffles per V-row step per warp (20 for kv, 20 for o) plus 5 per l2norm value (80 at T=8).
  New layout: a lane owns ONE V row (RPW float4 registers, K float4 index r*LPR+lk), LPR = 32/RPW lanes per row -> a reduction is log2(LPR) = 3 shuffles (NS=8) and the result is
  already on every lane of the row, no broadcast. 6 shuffles per step instead of 40. l2norm / final RMSNorm sums use a reduce-scatter ("transposed") warp sum (`tsum`): N-1+(5-log2 N)
  shuffles for N values instead of 5N (16 instead of 80 at T=8); same pairwise adds, so the sums are bitwise those of the butterfly.
- Measured (profile, same clocks/days, `code`): T=4 20.3 -> 18.0 us, T=8 29.2 -> 24.0 us (-0.15 ms/cycle, -0.7%). Registers 80..96 (T=4..8), no spills.
- Concluded: shuffles were a part, not the whole; the per-row slope at T=4->8 is still ~1.5 us/row. `try`: check PASS (all correctness checks), score 173.96 (kept 173.64) within noise.

## 2. Where the time goes (in-kernel clock64 probes, dumped by a static destructor to probe.txt; removed from the final source)
Averages over all blocks, SM cycles from block start, T=4 / T=8, after idea 1:
conv + pending rows + first barrier ~14.1k / 18.4k; l2norm +1.2k / +2.5k; replay (pc rank-1 rows + flush store) +2.3k / +2.6k; recurrence +3.1k / +5.1k (~770 cycles per row: issue bound, 4 FP ops per state element);
epilogue publish/atomic +1.5k, last-block RMSNorm tail +3.4k.  => the prologue, not the recurrence, was the biggest block (60% of the kernel).
Ablations via nsys (T=4 avg us): no epilogue 15.4, no replay+flush 13.0, no recurrence 13.9, prologue only 5.1 (state loads dead-code eliminated there).

## 3. Prologue restructuring
- Expected: SASS showed the three conv channels (q, k, v) executed strictly in sequence (load -> silu -> 12 STG.U16 of the new conv states -> next channel's loads, because the stores may alias the later loads), and the pending delta rows were loaded only after all of that (plain LDG -> STS, behind the stores).  So ~4 dependent memory round trips + 3 serial silu blocks.
- Change: (a) pending rows -> smem with cp.async issued right after reading cur/pend (no registers), (b) gating inputs (a, dt_bias, A_log, b) loaded before any st

# gemv2 lab notebook

## 1. Programmatic dependent launch (PDL) for the GEMVs
Expected: next GEMV's CTAs start early, prefetch weights into registers, `griddepcontrol.wait` before the activations -> hides launch gap/ramp/tail (~1-2 us x 320 GEMVs).
Measured: ptxas "griddepcontrol requires .target sm_90 or higher" -> not available on sm_86 (RTX 3090). Reverted. Concluded: dead on this hardware.

## 2. Cheaper k_w4 instruction stream (dequant lop3 merge + branch-free stream addressing)
Expected: GEMV_LOG says removing dequant+mma altogether gains 3.5-7%; main loop is ~230 SASS instr per 1 KB group, so a leaner loop should recover part of it.
Change (bit-identical numerics): (a) `(w>>4j & 0x000F000F) | 0x43004300` as ONE lop3 with both constants in registers (was and + or: 4 instr/pair -> 3); (b) the (tile, group) stream
as 32-bit element offsets with a select between `step` and `wrap` increments (the old setp() recomputed 64-bit tile pointers inside predicated blocks, ~20 issued instr per group);
(c) activation pointer = xbase + ct*KS*16 (no reset at tile end). SASS body per group ~234 -> ~160 lines, regs 92 -> 96.
Measured (full `try`, same machine state conditions, interleaved in time): kept 173.15 (clock 1650) vs change 176.71 (clock 1590-1620): **+2.06%**, check PASS.
Concluded: the kernel IS issue/latency sensitive; keep going on instruction count.
Re-measure of the same change (v1): 177.24 (clock 1605), baseline 173.15 -> +2.4% / +2.06% in two runs.

## 3. Rotating register sets (U+1 sets, no weight-register copies) + 32-bit running activation offset (v2)
Expected: removes the ~9 IMAD.MOV copies of the weight/scale registers per group and ~4 address instr; SASS loop smaller, regs 96 -> 77.
Measured: 173.69 (clock 1635, i.e. not power-limited) vs v1 re-run 177.24 -> **-2%**, check PASS. Reverted to v1 (mine_v1/).
Concluded: fewer instructions is not the whole story; the compiler's schedule with the copies (loads issued at body start, consumed copies) is better. Not investigated further.

## 4. Per-shape config re-sweep on the tile-contiguous layout (profile run, one instantiation per shape x config via a dummy template id; variant picked by weight-pointer hash so all variants run inside the same graph)
Expected: the table (w8k4u2 everywhere, w8k8u2 for q|k|v) was tuned on the old layout; KS=1/2 might now win (no tile-end smem reduce / syncs).
Measured (us per call, nsys, `code` prompt, calls/cycle ~15-27 each):
| shape | w8k4u2 | w8k2u3 | w8k1u3 |
| gate\|up 34816x5120 | **110.7** | 112.1 | 115.5 |
| down 5120x17408 | **55.9** | 56.9 | 84.2 |
| o_proj

# smallk lab notebook

## Baseline profile (try --profile, code prompt, 32 cycles, 21.66 ms/cycle wall)
k_w4 GEMVs 18.7 ms (86%), DeltaNet kernels 1.38 ms (dn T=4: 23 us x33, T=8: 41.6 us x15), k_bf16_small (in_proj_a|b, overlapped) 0.44, rmsnorm 0.385 (135 x 2.9 us), attention 0.43,
everything else (<0.1 ms). Kernel-time sum minus overlapped a|b is ~20.96 ms vs 21.66 wall: ~0.7 ms of launch gaps / host mailbox.

## Idea 1: deferred DeltaNet snapshots (replay accepted rows in the next step)
Expected: DN verify step writes T snapshots of 3.15 MB per layer (T=4: 12.6 MB, T=8: 25 MB); only the snapshot of the accepted row a-1 is ever read. Defer: a T>=2 step stores no state snapshots,
only its per-row recurrence inputs (norm k, v, exp(g), beta; 1 KB/row/head); the next step reads the base slot (cur-pend), replays the pend accepted rows in registers, writes slot cur once, and continues.
Traffic per layer per step 1 read + 1 write instead of 1 + T. Predicted -0.5 ms (T=4) .. -1.2 ms (T=8) per cycle = 2-5%.
(files: src/deltanet.cu ring kernel + flush, src/engine.cu, src/mtp_sample.h spec_finish(T), prefill.py flush at fast-prefill entry, snapshot flushes first.)
Measured (try, same session): full run 166.35 tok/s (code 170.4 prose 108.8 math 169.5 long8k 133.5 edit 228.4 table 221.0; pristine ~164.53, noise 0.11%), check PASS (all teacher-forced, forced-acceptance, sampler checks).
Profile after (code prompt): wall 21.661 -> 21.426 ms/cycle (-1.1%); dn_kernel T=4 23.0 -> 21.5 us, T=8 41.6 -> 31.2 us (all other kernels unchanged within 0.01 ms). Profile-run main 167.67 vs 165.86 before.
Concluded: kept. Gain is smaller than the traffic model (T=4: -450 MB/cycle predicted -0.5 ms, got -0.07): the kernel is latency / shuffle-bound, not bandwidth bound, so the replay's extra serial rows
(avg a rows x 20 shuffles each, 48 layers) eat most of the saved write time; T=8 (tail cycles on the copy-heavy prompts) gains most (-10 us x 48).
Side effects: +39 MB of row records (dn_rows); the 9-slot snapshot ring is now only used as 2-slot base/materialised pair (allocation unchanged).
Next (not done): transposed warp reduction (RPW values over 32 lanes in ~10 instead of 20 shuffles, bit-identical sums) to cut the DN shuffle load; smaller ring allocation.

# verify lineage notes

## Attempt 1: lazy DeltaNet snapshots (rank-1 delta ring)
- Expected: DeltaNet verify state traffic (1+T) x 3.15 MB -> 2 x 3.15 MB per layer (read base + write start state), deltas ~0.03 MB/row. T=4 DeltaNet 1.14 -> ~0.55 ms, T=8 2.0 -> ~0.6 ms (48 layers), i.e. ~3% of a T=4 cycle, ~7% of a T=8 cycle.
- Change: src/deltanet.cu kernel MODE 1/2 (replay pending rank-1 updates in smem while state load is in flight, bitwise same fp32 ops as the recurrence), delta buffer per layer (2 parities x 8 rows), ds[19]=pend (a | parity<<8) set by accept kernels / k_advance; materialize (all layers) before spec snapshot and python prefill. Contract of swiftmk_deltanet_step unchanged (MODE 0).
- Measured (try, full): v1 (parity ping-pong, write start state every step) 166.10 (+0.96%); T=4 DeltaNet kernel 23.7 -> 18.7 us/layer, T=8 41 -> 28 us. Not the ideal 10 us: latency chain (pend load -> state + delta loads -> replay -> rows).
- NS retune for lazy mode: T=3..4 NS=16: 22.4 us (worse), T=8 NS=16: 34 us (worse) -> keep NS=8.
- v2: linear append of delta rows (2 halves x 16 rows, pend = p | base<<8 | half<<12), start state written only when the buffer would overflow (every ~3 T=4 cycles). Full try: 167.37 tok/s (+1.7%), check PASS, code 171.6 / prose 109.6 / math 170.4 / long8k 134.5 / edit 229.7 / table 221.9.
- Concluded: kept v2. Remaining DeltaNet ~1.0 ms/cycle vs ~0.5 ms floor; next ideas: split the kernel latency chain (prefetch pending deltas before pend-dependent state loads), larger flush buffer.
